subject: HelioSearch — follow up + benchmark plan (Dedicated)
body:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex@heliosearch.ai>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya@heliosearch.ai>
Date: Wed, May 7, 2025 at 9:12 AM PDT
Subject: HelioSearch — follow up + benchmark plan (Dedicated)

Alex — thanks again for the quick context yesterday. Based on what you shared (rapid volume growth + periodic 429s during peak), I think it’s worth running a short Dedicated benchmark so you can see what “predictable throughput” looks like before we talk numbers.

Proposed plan (1 week end-to-end, usually faster):
1) 20-min SE deep dive: confirm workload shape + SLOs
   - model(s) + context lengths
   - traffic pattern (avg vs peak QPS / concurrency)
   - output lengths / streaming vs non-streaming
   - current pain points (429s, p95 latency, retries, cost)
2) Redwood runs an apples-to-apples benchmark on Dedicated capacity
   - measure TTFT + p50/p95 latency + tokens/sec + error rate under load
   - compare Hosted settings vs Dedicated settings (batching, max concurrency, queueing)
3) Review results + recommend a capacity shape (and whether “Dedicated” vs “Private/VPC” is the right end state)

If helpful, we can use either:
- Your prompts + expected response length distribution (best), or
- A sanitized prompt set you’re comfortable sharing

Scheduling: would either Thu 10:30am PT or Fri 1:00pm PT work for the SE deep dive? If easier, grab a slot here and I’ll align the right folks on our side:
https://calendly.com/redwood/heliosearch-dedicated-deep-dive

Attaching a quick Dedicated overview (2-pager) and a one-page benchmark template we typically use.

Attachment(s):
- Redwood_Dedicated_Overview_2025Q2.pdf (application/pdf)
- HelioSearch_Benchmark_Plan_v1.pdf (application/pdf)

Best,
Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
VP Sales, North America
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Chen <alex@heliosearch.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya@heliosearch.ai>
Date: Wed, May 7, 2025 at 4:27 PM PDT
Subject: Re: HelioSearch — follow up + benchmark plan (Dedicated)

Stephanie — this is great, thank you.

Fri 1:00pm PT works on our side.

A few details ahead of time:
- Current primary workload is chat completions for “search assistant” features.
- Typical input 2–6k tokens, but we have a long tail up to ~16k.
- Output generally 200–800 tokens.
- Spikes are tied to customer batch jobs (we can give you rough peak concurrency).
- Our biggest issue has been retry storms when we hit rate limits, which then pushes p95 way up.

We can share a sanitized prompt set + traffic distribution. Priya can send over something tomorrow.

One question: for Dedicated, do we get a hard throughput reservation (so we don’t see 429s except for misconfiguration), or is it still “best effort” just with higher limits?

Thanks,
Alex

Alex Chen
CTO, HelioSearch
alex@heliosearch.ai

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Chen <alex@heliosearch.ai>
Cc: Priya Desai <priya@heliosearch.ai>
Date: Wed, May 7, 2025 at 5:06 PM PDT
Subject: Re: HelioSearch — follow up + benchmark plan (Dedicated)

Perfect — I’ll send a calendar hold for Fri 1:00pm PT.

Re: Dedicated reservation: yes, the point of Dedicated is a reserved pool with predictable throughput and isolation. You can still get 429s if you exceed the agreed concurrency/throughput guardrails (or if there’s an application-level burst far beyond the reserved envelope), but it’s not “best effort shared capacity” like Hosted.

On Friday, we’ll align on:
- what you consider acceptable “peak” (so we size the reservation appropriately)
- what behavior you want when you exceed peak (queueing vs controlled shedding)
- retry guidance to avoid the cascade you mentioned

For the prompt set, if you can include these fields, we can run a clean benchmark quickly:
- ~50–100 representative prompts
- expected max_tokens / typical output length
- context-length histogram (even rough buckets are fine)
- desired region(s) (if you have any constraints)
- success criteria (e.g., p95 TTFT < X ms, sustained Y tok/s, <Z% errors)

See you Friday.

Best,
Stephanie
